content: Search engines organize information from documents so users can find relevant results quickly.
An inverted index maps each word to the documents where the word appears.
Document frequency counts how many documents contain a particular word.
Term frequency counts how many times a word occurs inside one document.
Computer science uses algorithms and data structures to solve search and indexing problems.
A hash map provides fast lookup for words, document identifiers, and frequencies.
Search ranking can use word frequency to determine which documents are more relevant.
The search engine reads documents, cleans words, builds an index, and returns matching documents.
